name: Battle of the Plains of Abraham

phases.title: Wolfe's line forms on the plateau
phases.text: Wolfe's army formed a line across the Plains, its right on the bluff above the St Lawrence and its left on a bluff and wood above the St Charles. Canadian militia and native sharpshooters engaged the left flank from the trees and scrub.

phases.title: Montcalm orders a general advance
phases.text: The French regulars moved against the British line. The British lines held their fire as the French approached.

phases.title: The British fire two volleys and the French break
phases.text: The French fired two disorganised volleys. The British then fired at close range, marched forward a few paces and fired a second general volley, which sent the attackers into retreat.

phases.title: The French retreat and the Highlanders pursue
phases.text: British troops fell into a disorganised pursuit of the retreating French. The 78th Fraser Highlanders followed with their swords and met heavy fire from the militia that remained in the trees.

phases.title: Bougainville's column arrives from the rear
phases.text: Townshend took charge and saw Bougainville's column approaching from the British rear. He formed two battalions from the confused troops and turned them to meet it.

phases.title: Bougainville retreats and the French cross the St Charles
phases.text: Bougainville did not attack and retreated. The rest of Montcalm's army slipped back across the St Charles, the militia holding the bridge.

note: The directions follow from the line's two ends: the right on the St Lawrence bluff and the left above the St Charles, so the British faced the city. The accounts do not say exactly where the wood, the houses and the bridge lay, so they are placed on the side the story needs. The plan does not show the British light infantry in the rear, and it treats the 'two battalions facing north' and the left wing as one block.
